assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read in full with its front matter: the canonical V2 character monograph SHINEPOST_V2_NANAMI_E01_E12_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (SPV2-CH-NANAMI, version 0.3, 19,043 bytes), a retrospective portrait of the Japanese television anime E01-E12 through the final Brightest office decision, located by observation, claim, adjudication and production-form IDs (SPV2-OBS, SPV2-CLM, SPV2-ADJ, SPV2-PF) and by seconds into each episode, with an E12 audience-attribution erratum. Its author read the accepted episode records with the whole season available and did no new viewing or listening. The episode readings, ledgers and source adjudications it links are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them. No primary source, performed voice or supplementary material was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Located appearances across Japanese TV E01-E12. Before the series: the rival-period preparation of Yukine and Momiji after Yuki's proposal, which Yuki has told her about (shown in E08, 1033.33-1152.07 s), belongs to her knowledge throughout, though how much Yuki disclosed is unknown. E01: expected for a lesson. E05: back early from an FFF recording, the requested harder session, the farm shoot with Rio for Director Sato, and the conversation with Naoki. E09: Yukine invokes her training in addressing Haru; Nanami is not shown delivering the invitation. E10: a probable appearance as presenter at an FFF NEXT STEP event where TINGS open (no credited line). E12: in the Nakano audience, with tears at 923.339 s. State label Nanami@E12, after Nakano and the final Brightest decision; her role in the five's future is unknown. Her childhood, recruitment and private history are not given.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy, which bears on this record only by leaving the B/C rulings unchanged. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph names one variable that changes what help she gives: her relationship to the particular task. Conducting a session her pupils have asked to make harder, she makes a direct demand that they get back up (E05). Co-presenting on camera with a novice, she carries the exchange, makes a small correction usable and leaves the novice room to contribute (E05 farm: the tomato correction, the word for mouth). After the director's decision, she quietly turns Naoki's attention toward Rio without promising editorial control (E05, 971.512-978.102 s). In the audience she can only watch, imagining specific mistakes for specific pupils, and is in tears (E12). Concern for a junior and a presenter's duty to the farmer and the director predict the same acts, so the monograph declines to read private affection off the recording; that is productive uncertainty. Not B: each value of the variable rests on one located occasion, the range is professional only, and the source gives no account of why she first wanted the work or how she reconciles her career with teaching. Not D: the portrait is dedicated, located and states its own conditional predictions with support labels and an altering condition.

Her positions are located across the season: instructor expected for a lesson (E01), senior on camera and trainer (E05), preparer of a rival plan others chose (shown in E08), probable presenter at an FFF event (E10), spectator in tears (E12). Not C: the monograph traces a change of position relative to her pupils, from keeping them practicing to watching them perform, not a sequence of states in her with causes. Not E: the positions are dedicated, located observations across five episodes.

The monograph describes register by function rather than by attested wording: the familiar ナオくん to Naoki and an ironic reply when he praises her group's success; a direct demand to two trainees who asked to be pressed harder; a public greeting at the farm whose linked clauses a novice can echo; one correct word supplied on camera before a mistake hardens. It says none of this requires an inference from an uninspected inflection. Not C: almost no Japanese wording of hers is quoted beyond the address form, the row claims no SPEECH, and there is no sustained private speech. Not E: the register functions are located by scene and addressee.

Only glimpses: Haru's delighted embrace when Nanami arrives early from a recording (Haru's initiative), the ease with which she teases Naoki, and her nerves as a spectator. The monograph states that there is almost no sustained private speech at home, no stated hobbies and no habitual food choices; her taste in vegetables at the farm is professional appraisal, not a stated preference. Not D: these are a few located moments, not distributed evidence.

Distinct located stances with reasons: to Yukine and Momiji, the instructor they expect and ask to press them harder, who prepared them for a rival plan Yuki proposed and they accepted (E05, E08); to Rio, a senior on camera who scaffolds a junior's contribution (E05); to Naoki, an old acquaintance addressed as ナオくん, offered an FFF submanager post she does not press when he declines, and urged to tell the girls about his past work (E05); to Haru, the object of a delighted welcome (E05). Training and introducing give her no authority over TINGS's management, bookings or lineup. Not B: each relationship is sampled in one or two scenes, and how much private affection underlies her help cannot be separated from professional duty. Not D: the stances are differentiated and explained by her position in each relationship.

One located inner state: at Nakano she pictures Yukine missing choreography and Momiji forgetting words, is reminded she is not the one going on stage, and is in tears at 923.339 s (E12). The monograph says her precise evaluation of each step, her private judgment of the rival strategy, when the tears began, what she understood of Rio's feelings and why she wanted this work are unavailable. Not D: this is one scene of stated and visible feeling.

One located disagreement: she and Naoki differ over whether he should trade on his past to earn the girls' trust; she states her view and does not persist when he keeps his position (E05). She does not contest the director's decision about Rio's tasting; Sato and Naoki settle the cut. Not D: a single mild disagreement.
The row claims no ETHICS, and the monograph locates no weighing of moral alternatives by her. Whether she judged the rival plan or its possible harm to Haru is stated to be unknown.

Two located instances of professional wit: on camera she turns Rio's mispronunciation of tomato into an occasion to credit the second try (E05), and off camera she treats Naoki's praise of her group as ironic coming from him (E05). The monograph notes the written source does not establish the exact sound of the tomato joke. Not D: two moments, both inside work.

One dedicated, separately reviewed portrait at the E12 boundary (version 0.3, 19,043 bytes), located to observation, claim and adjudication IDs and seconds, with an audience-attribution erratum applied. Not B: it is a compact portrait of a sparse presence (E01, E05, E08, E09 by reference, E10 probable, E12); its author did no new viewing or listening; and the readings and ledgers it rests on are not curated on this subject. Not D: it is dedicated, reviewed and located.

Affirmative located limits and refused readings: no credit for a new training method and no blame for Rio's difficulty with balance, since Rio trains in another room (E05); no evidence she procured the E10 booking or spoke an introduction there; no authority over TINGS's management, bookings or lineup; Kei, not Nanami, is the caller about the single and the lyric (E05); the extent of Yuki's disclosure about Haru is unknown (E08); private affection cannot be read off the recording; the Nakano reassurer's identity stays open; no romantic or intimate history with Naoki or anyone else is established. Not A: the evidence marks these gaps without explaining them. Not C: they are located findings, not inferences from silence.

Claims are placed by episode and seconds; the rival-period preparation shown in E08 is kept as prior knowledge; the E10 appearance is marked probable; the Nakano tears are timed; the state label is Nanami@E12 after the final Brightest decision. Not A: her history before the series and her role after E12 are unknown. Not C: placements are precise and uncertain attributions are flagged.

scenario_readiness.note: The curated portrait describes what her speech does in a few professional scenes but quotes almost none of it, and states that the source gives almost no sustained private speech; the row claims no SPEECH. That does not constrain generated lines enough for even bounded illustrative use.

conditions: The monograph's own case: after Nakano, a novice in a fresh farm segment freezes after a greeting, with recording under way, an available prompt and a familiar assignment. Predict that she continues the exchange herself, makes a small correction usable and leaves the novice room to contribute (strong grounds, per the monograph).

If the director then rejects a take and the novice blames herself for the whole shoot: moderate support for quietly turning the manager's attention toward the novice, without promising editorial control or assuring her about what viewers will see.
If trainees have personally asked for a difficult exercise in a session she conducts: a direct demand for another effort.
In the audience, with no working responsibility: concern, with no precedent for intervening.
Juniors other than Rio, Yukine and Momiji are a lower-confidence transfer; strangers, management decisions and bookings are not supported.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Nanami@E12, after Nakano and the final Brightest decision, with the rival-period preparation known to her; or a source-near variant of one located E05 scene that states the changed element. How much Yuki told her about Haru, and her role in the five's future, are unknown and are not to be filled in.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Yukine and Momiji as pupils; Rio as a junior on camera; Naoki as an old professional acquaintance; Director Sato and a farmer as working counterparts; a comparable novice only under the lower-confidence transfer.

No management, booking or lineup decision for TINGS; no private or domestic setting; no romance; no cross-series setting.

known_limits.statement: Each condition in her model rests on one located occasion: one requested hard session (E05), one location shoot with a novice (E05), one quiet cue to Naoki after the director's decision (E05) and one audience (E12).
Concern for a junior and a presenter's duty to the farmer and the director produce the same acts, and the monograph says the degree of private affection cannot be read off the recording.

Training two girls and being able to introduce a group to a concert audience confer no general authority over TINGS's management, bookings or lineup; no evidence shows she procured the E10 booking or spoke a credited introduction there.

How much Yuki disclosed to her about Haru's prior group, the conditions of Haru's return or the possibility of emotional harm is unknown, so her interventions are not a judgment on the whole rival plan.

The monograph's author read the accepted episode records and did no new viewing or listening; the written source does not establish the exact sound of the tomato joke, and the Nakano reassurer's identity stays open.
No romantic or intimate history is established with Naoki or anyone else.
Her home life, hobbies, habitual food choices, childhood, recruitment and reasons for wanting this work are not given in the source the portrait covers.
Her role in the five's future after the Budokan decision, including any further coaching or booking, is unknown.
